newsitem.title: JAPAN: Akai enjoys better-than-expected interim earnings.
newsitem.headline: Akai enjoys better-than-expected interim earnings.

text.p: Audio-visual equipment maker Akai Electric Co Ltd reported unexpectedly good first-half business results on Monday, saying restructuring had helped it outperform the industry average.

Akai, controlled by Hong Kong's Semi-Tech (Global) Co Ltd 0448. HK group, posted a parent current profit of 418 million yen ($3.73 million) in the six months to September 30, having forecast a loss for the period of 500 million yen ($4.46 million) earlier this year.

"We posted an interim current profit because of increased profitability, cost-cutting efforts and reduced interest payments as a result of new share issue in June and an issue of warrant bonds in July," the company said in a statement.

It said its half-year sales were 24.13 billion yen ($215 million), up from its forecast of 20 billion yen ($178 million) earlier this year, due to larger-than-expected sales, especially of television sets, as a result of aggressive marketing.

"The global electrical appliance industry was facing difficulties with demand for the majority of products slow (in the first half). But despite such circumstances, we were mostly able to achieve our restructuring targets and to show a better performance than the industry average," Akai said.

In 1995, suffering losses due to severe competition, Akai allocated new shares to three affiliates of Semi-Tech for $172 million, making Semi-Tech the largest shareholder, with a stake of about 55 percent.
Akai revised up its outlook for 1996/97 parent earnings in October, having already made an upward revision last month.
It now expects a profit of 1.7 billion yen ($15.1 million) on sales of 60 billion yen ($535 million).
In October, it predicted a parent current profit of 1.00 billion yen ($8.9 million) and sales of 53.50 billion yen ($477 million).
Comparable figures were not available for 1995 as Akai has changed its accounting period. ($1=112)
